analysis:
This batch contains only documentation changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/ssd-ledger-charge-per-donation.md) and an edit to docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md at head lines ~390-400, plus a date bump at line 3. No executable source is supplied, so the underlying SSDWriteBehind.chargeWholeDonation implementation is not visible and was not reviewed.

The docs describe a behavior change: an attention donation of several blocks now reserves the summed DBK3 size in one write-budget charge before its first write. If that charge is refused, it falls back to per-block charging, so the leading blocks that fit are still written. Charges stay prior to writes and are never refunded. Skipped blocks stay charged, which is conservative toward the daily cap rather than permissive.

Relevant threat: T-041, which covers the SSD tier's wear and endurance bounds and the at-rest posture. As described, the change keeps the daily write cap as an upper bound on application cache-file writes. The ledger still records only time buckets and byte counts, with no keys, tokens or model identifiers, so the leak #2 posture is unchanged. TTL, HMAC naming, encryption and the per-donation adoption gate are untouched by the documentation.

Open integration question: the code is not in this batch. The next pass should verify that chargeWholeDonation (a) cannot under-charge relative to the actual serialized DBK3 sizes of the blocks written, for example through per-block size estimates or overflow in the summation, (b) never writes a block beyond what was reserved, and (c) still fails closed when the ledger is corrupt or inaccessible. The documentation describes these as intended, but they are not verified here. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
